summary: FERC dismisses the July 2026 rehearing and clarification requests on the E-7 show cause order, finding the order made only preliminary findings and is not final, and declines to give guidance while the proceeding is in abeyance until November 16, 2026.

points.point: FERC says rehearing lies only from a final order, and the show cause order did not make a final decision on the tariff.
points.quote: The Commission did not make any final decision or determination in the Show Cause Order on

points.point: The order determined only that the tariff appears unjust, and opened a section 206 proceeding to reach a final determination.
points.quote: The Commission determined only that the Tariff appears to be unjust, unreasonable, and unduly discriminatory or preferential and instituted an FPA section 206 show cause proceeding to reach a final determination on this issue.

points.point: FERC dismisses the clarification requests too and will not give guidance while the proceeding is in abeyance.
points.quote: We do not intend to provide clarification or guidance with respect to the Show Cause Order while the show cause proceeding is held in abeyance.

points.point: Show cause responses are due November 16, 2026 and answers December 16, 2026, as set in the August abeyance order.
points.quote: responses to the Show Cause Order will be due on November 16, 2026, and answers to responses will be due on December 16, 2026.

points.point: FERC encourages PJM, the Transmission Owners and stakeholders to keep developing section 205 proposals.
points.quote: We encourage PJM, the Transmission Owners, and stakeholders to continue with the development of one or more FPA section 205 proposals.

throughLine.text: Disposes of rehearing requests on the E-7 order's flexible load, cost recovery and definition findings by treating them as preliminary, leaving those issues to the November 2026 filings.
